title: The problem of evil and theodicy
note: The problem of evil is the main argument against God. The logical version says God and evil are incompatible; Plantinga's free will defense is widely judged to answer it. The evidential version says seemingly pointless suffering makes God unlikely; replies include theodicies (free will, soul-making, natural law) and skeptical theism. A defense shows possible reasons; a theodicy, actual ones.

read.title: Mackie, Plantinga, and Rowe
text: J. L. Mackie argued in 1955 that theism is not merely unproven but inconsistent. His logical problem can be set out:

(1) God is omnipotent, omniscient, and wholly good. (2) A wholly good being prevents evil as far as it can. (3) An omnipotent, omniscient being can prevent all evil. (4) So if God exists, there is no evil. (5) There is evil. (6) So God does not exist.

Alvin Plantinga's free will defense targets premise (2). A world with creatures who are significantly free, able to do right or wrong, may be better than a world of puppets. But God cannot cause free creatures to do only what is right, or they would not be free. It is possible, then, that God could not create a world with free creatures and no moral evil. Since it is only meant to show consistency, this is a defense, not a theodicy. Many philosophers, including some atheists, judge that it answers the logical problem.

William Rowe shifted to an evidential argument. Consider a fawn burned in a forest fire, dying slowly with no one ever knowing. (1) There probably are such evils that an all-good, all-powerful God could prevent without losing a greater good. (2) Such a God would prevent them. (3) So probably God does not exist.
Skeptical theists such as Stephen Wykstra reply that our inability to see a reason gives little evidence that there is none, since God's reasons may lie beyond our grasp.

q.q: Which premise of Mackie's argument does the free will defense target?
Why is the free will defense called a defense, not a theodicy?

It gives God's actual reasons for every evil
